title: #16 D-098: a round-start replay that conflicts ends the round at once as a free conflict round with the branch at its start point
objective: When replaying a ticket's own commits at the start of a round conflicts, that round ends before any agent starts as a free merge round, with the conflicting branch restarted at its start point and its old head kept under refs/devloop/before-rebase/ for the next worker or verifier.
outline: devloop/ticket_issuer.py: the previous ticket's round-start step (suggested name rebase_round) returns the conflicts instead of putting both branches back. Per conflicted branch: keep its head before the replay under refs/devloop/before-rebase/t<N>-r<r> or .../t<N>-cases-r<r> (`git update-ref <ref> <old> ''`, i.e. create only; on failure try '-2', '-3', ...); set the branch to its start point (`reset --hard <start>` in the worktree that has it); t/<N>-cases conflicting means t/<N>'s start is the target's head and t/<N>'s own commits still exclude the old cases head. In _round(): when the step reports conflicts, self._free = 'merge', one self.save() (branch_base, one 'rebase conflict' event per branch, cases = None on a cases conflict) and `return text, costs` before any agent starts; one_round() then sets worker_ok false as for any feedback, and go() counts the round as free through free_rounds(). integrate(): only the text of the step-6 conflict feedback changes (item 5); the ownership checks added by #131 stay where they are. Nothing in board.py changes (merge_failed keys on 'merging the latest ' and ' failed ('). Docs per item 6. Never move the target, main or any int/ branch here; only t/<N> and t/<N>-cases and the new refs are written (refs/devloop/* is never pushed).

Fixture commits and groups exactly as the previous ticket's test plan describes (side worktree per commit, self.add(...), tx.put_group({...}) with 'created' and 'history'); res = self.controller(), rc 0. The round-2 worker's prompt is <tmp>/wt/runs/1/r2-worker/prompt.md (agents.start writes prompt.md in the run dir); the feedback text is read there because a landed ticket's 'feedback' list is emptied at merge. Item 3 copies T100Acceptance.test_8's fixture (self.config(max_rounds=1), two tickets in g1, plan 'shared') and picks the ticket whose state is stuck. Run once: test_issuer and test_board_tickets (its merge_failed cases use their own literals and must stay green); no existing case is expected to change - T100Acceptance.test_8 keeps its assertions (the loser's round 2 now ends at the replay conflict, still a free merge round, still stuck 'rounds' at round 2); name any case you change.

M5 accepted cases on t/1-cases conflict (add/add cases/case_1.txt) with int/g1: the same 6 worker rounds, then stuck. M4 (request item 4, the fixer): main moved during the group's first full run; the regression went red and the controller started the fixer in the same step without follow_main (no 'main moved' group event before 'fix round 1'), but auto_fixer.fix() merged main into int/g1 before the fixer agent started (the agent's HEAD contained main, top commit "Merge branch 'main' into int/g1"; on a conflict the agent is told to merge it). So a fix round already starts from the latest main; no change is needed there. Git (2.43.0 here), measured in a throwaway repo: `git rebase --onto <new target> <base>` on a ticket branch that merged its old target replays the commits that merge brought in ('work 6' of another ticket reached the new group): dropping the merge commit is not enough, so the request's literal command is not used. `git rev-list --reverse --first-parent --no-merges <branch> --not <base> <old target> <new target> [<old cases head>]` lists exactly the ticket's own commits. `git rebase -i --empty=drop --onto S S` with GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR copying a written todo ('pick <sha>' lines) replays that list, drops a commit that became empty (rc 0), keeps the same shas when nothing changes, and on a conflict exits 1 with the unmerged paths in `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`; `git rebase --abort` puts the branch back on its old head with a clean tree. An empty todo makes rebase -i exit 1 ('nothing to do'): with no own commits use `git reset --hard S` instead. cherry-pick on 2.43 stops on a commit that became empty (rc 1, 'now empty'), so it needs --skip handling if used. Design decisions: the conflict round ends before any agent (rather than running the worker in the same round) so the round counts exactly like today's step-6 conflict round - free, with the resolving worker in the next, counted round; the kept head lives under refs/devloop/before-rebase/ next to refs/devloop/dropped/ and is never pushed; a cases conflict throws the cases out because only the verifier may write them (the worker must not) and the verifier prompt has no feedback section, so it writes them again from the ticket on the restarted branch. Depends on the previous ticket (it replaces that ticket's interim 'put both branches back'). Group g11, same reasons as the previous ticket; #131 (ownership checks in integrate()) has landed, so the step-6 text edit has no open neighbour.

(implementer) After a conflict round: the branch that conflicted is at its start point (the target's head; for t/<N>, the rebased t/<N>-cases head when t/<N> held the cases and their replay succeeded), with no rebase in progress and a clean worktree; branch_base[<branch>] is the target's head; the history has one event 'rebase conflict' with branch, onto (the target) and kept (the ref); a conflict on t/<N>-cases also sets the ticket's cases to null so the verifier writes them again; the target and main do not move; when the ref name exists already, '-2', '-3', ... is appended (first free); when both branches conflict, one round ends with both texts joined by a newline; the next round starts the worker (worker_ok is false). request:
# New work starts from the latest verified point (docs/DECISIONS.md D-098; follow-up of GitHub issue #16)

The user's rule (2026-11-24, verbatim in D-098): 「反正我希望group 跑完驗證後 新的實作 都是基於那個點 ，後續的commit 都要先rebase 或是基於最新驗證過的點往後寫， 這是我的大原則」. Read D-097 and D-098 first, and the open tickets #134 #135 #136 (group g11), which change what happens to a stuck ticket's group; place this work so it does not conflict with them (core/chain.py; depend on them where it touches the same code). Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ using loop_harness.py; each case runs in seconds.

What the main session read in the code (inference, not measured; measure it first and write what you find in the ticket):
- devloop/core/gitx.py `Git.worktree(path, branch, start)`: when the branch t/N already exists it is checked out as it is; `start` is used only for a new branch. devloop/ticket_issuer.py `go()` calls it with start=target once, then runs rounds; the ticket branch takes in the target only at the end of a round (step 6, "take in the latest target ... move the target").
- So a retried ticket (stuck, then readied) and a ticket moved to another group (`actl dag move`, `actl new --revise` with a dag part, D-097's ungrouped ticket later placed) keep the base they were made from. A worker writes on an old base, and for a moved ticket the old group's commits that were never verified come along when it merges into its new group (T: #320's branch was made from g63's int branch, then #320 was put in g88).

Wanted:
1. Before every round's agent starts (worker, and the verifier's cases branch where it has one), the ticket branch is rebased onto the current head of its target (the group's int branch, which already takes main when a group lands: ticket_controller.py follow_main). Only the ticket's own commits are replayed: the commits on t/N (and t/N-cases) that are not on the base it was last put on. Record that base on the ticket (e.g. `base` sha written when the branch is made or rebased) so a later rebase can use `git rebase --onto <target> <base>`; for a branch made before this change with no recorded base, use the merge-base with the branch's old target if it is known, else with the new target.
2. A ticket that changes group (any path) or comes back to ready after stuck: at its next round its branch is rebased onto the new target with only its own commits (as 1); commits of the old group that are not on the new target never reach it. If the ticket's own commits include merges of its old target (step 6 of an earlier round), those merges are not replayed.
3. A rebase with conflicts is aborted and handled like today's merge conflict when taking in the target: the worker gets the conflict to resolve on a branch that starts from the new target, and the round counts as a conflict round (free, as today). Never force anything onto the target or main; only t/N and t/N-cases are rewritten (they are devloop's own branches, nobody else's checkout).
4. The fixer (auto_fixer on a group's int branch) already works on the group's branch after follow_main; check that a fix round starts only after the group's branch has taken in the latest main (follow_main ran for that main sha), and say in the ticket whether that already holds.
5. Document in devloop/README.md: "every round starts from the latest verified point" with what is rebased, when, and what happens on conflict.
- removes: work on a stale base; a moved ticket carrying another group's unverified commits.
- Out of scope: rebasing int branches (they keep merging main; they are shared by the group's tickets); changing how a group lands.
